notes.title: OUT NOW! - Just Flip Mode
notes.notes:
It's here!  A new way to play "That Flipping Mountain".

[previewyoutube=5ZKNk1zp-Ik;full][/previewyoutube]

Just Flip Mode is a free additional game play mode for "That Flipping Mountain".  After selecting "New Game" you will be presented with the option to play the "Standard Mode" or the new "Just Flip Mode"

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/06d78cd2ec7913a863e255152f48f64fccad867d.png[/img]

The new Just Flip Mode is recommended only after you've gained considerable experience with "Standard Mode".

With Just Flip Mode, you will play That Flipping Mountain with a single button.  Press to start jumping, then press/release to control your flip as you auto jump your way up the mountain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/3512108f1c9c976202f1f7b3953c3a6dccc6c92a.jpg[/img]

You'll need to stay very focused. Unlike in standard mode, if you fail to stick a landing in Just Flip Mode, you are "dead" and must restart at the beginning. (Permadeath!).

Don't worry, it's not quite as bad as it sounds... you don't need to flip all the way up the mountain with zero failures, there are 4 save points along the way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/badc7eb523a114d640ddc2532537409b428932f5.jpg[/img]

Once you pass a save point, the save point becomes your new starting position.

Finally, for this new Just Flip Mode, I've added 2 new achievements.

Get to the top of the mountain in Just Flip Mode and you get the following achievemnt:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/07f7a83fa30bdc277d98c11fde65171535ac867e.jpg[/img]

If you are slightly crazy you might try getting to the top of the mountian in Just Flip Mode with ZERO failed jumps.  If you do that you get this: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/d4521ec1a4743ec6d9018f0666c5f58567803176.jpg[/img]

I hope you enjoy the new game play mode! 

If you have any problems and/or questions please let me know in the forums.

Also, tell your friends about the game and encourage you favorite streamers to stream it. Helps immensely!

-Jeff

notes.title: Developer Notes #1: Release Week, Thanks, and Shoutout to Slovakia
notes.notes:
Hey Everyone.

First I'd like to give a huge thank you to everyone who has taken "That Flipping Mountain" (TFM) for a spin.  It is SO appreciated.

[h1]The Marketing Plan[/h1]
To be honest, I didn't really have a marketing plan for TFM. I'm one person without a ton of spare cash laying around for Marketing.  Given that TFM was heavily inspired by "Getting Over It" and "Jump King" I thought it'd make a good game for streaming. 
With that in mind, I decided to use a steam key service ([url=https://keymailer.co/]Keymailer[/url]) to send Steam keys to just about every streamer I could find who had also streamed "Getting Over It", "Jump King", "Pogostuck", or a handful of other difficult games.

[h1]The Marketing Results[/h1]
I'm very happy with how this worked.  For a small, relatively unknown game developer I had quite a few streamers give the game a go.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/d2eeb45cb0e0c3e85ed912ec954e1659a916a046.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/68ef820bc538571b6b48e75f77d8cba3c949c045.png[/img]

[h1]Special Shout-out to Slovakia[/h1]
Something amazing happened with Slovakia.  Both the #1 ([url=https://www.twitch.tv/resttpowered]resttpowered[/url]) and #2 ([url=https://www.twitch.tv/2sekundovymato]2sekundovymato[/url]) Twitch streamers played TFM for multiple hours over multiple sessions.  They both beat the game. At one point I even noticed the #1 streamer was watching/reacting to the #2 streamer as he played.

Here is one of  my favorite clips of the game from 2sekundovymato:
https://www.twitch.tv/2sekundovymato/clip/TrappedTiredRadishM4xHeh-28OswgfF3zjZwDRj

Below you can see how these two streamers drove Slovakia to be #1 in sales for TFM over the 1st week. As a one-man-team, with very little marketing budget, this was SO appreciated.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/1a40a0e1f755d8045682a56cfb0ccc10c5d78598.png[/img]

Thanks as well to all the smaller Slovakian streamers who also took the time to play the game on their channel.

[h1]Learning and Mastering the Controls[/h1]

The game-play controls for TFM evolved quite a bit over the 4 or so years of spare-time development.  I watched a lot of TFM Twitch streams and was happy to see that most players, with practice, were able to learn and sometimes master the controls.  I really wanted the controls to be easy to understand, but also be something you had to learn and gain skill in and I think I succeeded in that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/2c710eb069b94249933344d86bfd080b1ed5c449.gif[/img]

[h1]What's Next?[/h1]
In short, what's next is more "That Flipping Mountain". :-)  

I don't currently have any plans for a new game. I still have a lot of ideas for TFM and plan to role out some content updates, feature updates, quality of life updates, and  of course bug-fixes over the next year or so.  Remember I'm a one-man team doing this in my spare time so the new update won't be out tomorrow. :-)

What should be out fairly soon is TFM Steam Achievements.  I already started working on these and it has been going smoothly so far.

[h1]Finally, a Request for Assistance.[/h1]
If you have enjoyed playing and/or streaming "That Flipping Mountain" please spread the word to your friends and other streamers.  Word of mouth marketing is the best kind and anything you can do to help with that would be awesome!

Take Care,

-Jeff

notes.title: Refresh all the things!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone.  First I want to say thanks to all those who continue to follow the progress of this game. It is very much appreciated.

[h2]New Name[/h2]
Let's get right to the point.  As you probably noticed, 'Just Flip' has a new name:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/6e2d75ce6cefac2c6370c818db74a0e8dabb3ed3.png[/img]

I fully understand some will hate the new name, some will like it, and some will be indifferent.  That is all fine.  I just feel this name better fits what the game will be and 'Just Flip' was ultimately too generic.  Plus, I think some may be uttering these words under their breath once they start playing. :-)

Along with the rename, I have updated the Steam page with new logos, a new trailer and new screenshots.

[h2]Updated Graphics[/h2]
This isn't super new as I have posted a screen or two in the past, but I continue to try making 'That Flipping Mountain' look better.  Graphics are not my strong point so this is one of the more challenging aspects of game development for me. I do think it's starting to look decent, though.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/fd0415325a55d457beacadfc168c10af45188abe.png[/img]

[h2]New Mechanic: Diving and Water[/h2]
Prior to starting development on 'That Flipping Mountain', I was working on a  follow-up to an old diving game of mine called 'Diver' and 'Diver 2'.  I still plan to make that follow-up someday, but for now I decided to just bring the water system I had created for that game into this one.

I had been thinking about how to do this for quite a while. One of the key components of 'That Flipping Mountain' is that the controls are simple but the game is challenging. I think I finally figured out how to add the water and not break that tenant of the game.

It's actually pretty straightforward.  Some waterholes are not really obstacles, they are just something you can fall into. :-) If you do fall in, you can just launch yourself back out of the water. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/39abcce3445713414cf7755ea40c0d33e7a0ee3a.gif[/img]

Other waterholes ARE obstacles. For these, as seen in the GIF below, you will need to do a proper dive into the water. Once you do a proper dive, the swimming mechanic will kick-in and take you where you need to go.  You will then need to manage the flip out of the water and stick the landing. (Very similar to how the skiing works.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/6548cd88261b4cd1d037313fd64fc90e3bbc6ff0.gif[/img]

[h2]No more hand-holding[/h2]
Until  now, 'That Flipping Mountain' incorporated a very subtle assist when sticking a landing.  Essentially, when the character got close to the ground, the game would help line things up to make sticking the landing slightly easier. 
While this worked most of the time, occasionally it would make things feel "faked".  I thought the game would be to difficult without this, but as a test I removed it and played for a while.  I didn't notice a difference so I removed it. 
This game just takes a bit of practice. Once you get a feel for the inertia of the flip, sticking the landing gets easier. I think the assist is just un-necessary. Physics for the win!

[h2]Release Strategy[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/d5f105db9b3616b94f09ce8d396856b925ccb91a.png[/img]

For me, this game has been the most challenging game to position for release.  The market for games has changed so much in recent years. It's difficult to stand out.
I decided to not overthink things too much and just go with my gut.  For this reason, I'm going back to my original plan to release 'That Flipping Mountain' into Early Access and use that time to build out the mountain, get feedback, and refine all the things.

That about wraps it up for this post.  No that most these changes are behind me, I plan do concentrate more on building out the actual mountain.  I'll try to post more often to keep everyone up to date on my progress.

notes.title: Dev Blog 7: Slow But Steady Progress
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

Just a quick update to let you know I'm still working on 'Just Flip' everyday and making slow but steady progress. As I've mentioned in other posts, I make games in my spare time so things don't always move as fast as I'd like them to.

I did  recently shift some of my time over to my previous game, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/740230/Just_Ski/]Just Ski[/url], in order to put out a major update, but now I'm back to Just Flip and will be until it's released.

[h1]UPDATES[/h1]

[h2]Auto Jumping[/h2]
In my last post, I mentioned I was considering a big change to the game play for Just Flip. I was thinking about making the game auto jump rather than having the player pull-back, aim, and release.

After some play-testing, I decided against this and instead will just add auto-jump sections to the game. This way there will be a mix of auto-jumping and manual jumping.

[h2]Visuals[/h2]
When I updated Just Ski, I made some major improvements to the visuals.  I took what I learned from doing that update and applied it, with improvements, to Just Flip.

Here is a quick view of how things are looking right now.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/1be358715a42b575a7863ab08fc62808f9bef449.png[/img]

[h2]Editor Tools and Tweaks[/h2]
The other thing I've been working on a lot is editor tools for building out the mountain. The mountain in this game is going to be quite large so I need to have some tools in place to make it easier/quicker to build.  More on that in future posts.

I'm working steadily to get the game to a point where building out the content is all that remains.  You should see more frequent posts and updates once I get to that point,

Thanks for reading!

-Jeff

notes.title: Something I'm Considering
notes.notes:
Hey everyone.

A while back I created something for Just Flip that I call "Parkour Stones". They are very similar to the springs, but slightly quicker.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/b4a9a956144b554641e4b950a1220c5c94ac9cf3.gif[/img]

They turned out to be a whole lot of fun. So much so that I'm considering pivoting the game-play for 'Just Flip' to utilize the idea more heavily.

My thought process has gone something like this:

[i]The launch mechanic where you pull-back, aim, and then jump, doesn't seem to add a lot to the game. It's not the challenging part of the game and it isn't really the fun part.  Jumping is the fun part.

So, what if I ditched the entire pull-back, aim, jump mechanic and just let the little guy go nuts, parkour-style.[/i]

This change would actually make 'Just Flip' a ONE BUTTON, still very challenging, physics game.

Here is what that would look like. I would love to hear your thoughts.

https://youtu.be/s7uw49P9ABs

-Jeff

notes.title: Dev Blog 6: Good News/Bad News - Rethinking the Release Strategy.
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/b4a9a956144b554641e4b950a1220c5c94ac9cf3.gif[/img]

Hello everyone.

As I've  been working slowly but surely toward an early access release, I've come to the decision to change my release strategy for Just Flip.

I think this is both good news and bad news.  

[h1]What is changing?[/h1]
Instead of releasing to Early Access, I will be using demos and beta testing to get feedback for the game. 

[h1]Bad News First[/h1]
Since I'm not releasing to Early Access, I'll need a bit more time to build out the "Mountain", gather feedback, and prepare for a full, conventional release.  My new guess is that Just Flip's full release will be in Early 2021.  
I really, really wanted a 2020 release, but I'm a realist and I always want to be up-front with where things are.

[h1]The Good News[/h1]
A new, much more representative demo is coming soon... to Steam this time. This demo will be part of Steam's Autumn Festival.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/bb32885e762e1e05106555a73ebd8aee2393d65b.jpg[/img]

The Autumn Festival is set to run from Oct. 7th to Oct. 13th, but for those reading this, a little tip:

[i]The Just Flip demo will actually be released on Sept 23rd, a couple weeks ahead of the festival. You'll be able to grab it directly from the Just Flip Steam page and get a head start on the flipping.[/i]

[h1]Why The Change?[/h1]
The biggest reason for the change is I just don't think Early Access is the best fit for this style of game or my one-man, spare-time development "team". I'm not sure I'd be able to keep up with the required release pace and user feedback. I hear it can become a bit overwhelming.

I think getting feedback via demos and beta releases will be a better fit.  I'll have a call for beta testers later this year and I don't plan to be to stringent on who can join.

I hope everyone understands and as always feedback and comments are welcome.

-Jeff

notes.title: Dev Blog: Early Access Update 1
notes.notes:
Hey everyone as I work toward the 'Just Flip' launch to Early Access I thought I'd try to give periodic updates for those interested.

One of the primary things I've worked on lately is a re-do of the 1st 10 minutes or so of the game.  I had designed the beginning of the game prior to adding support for the spring jumps and skiing so none of that existed at the beginning of the game.

After playing with the springs and skiing for a while now, I've come to the conclusion that they really are the "star" of the game.  Therefore, it makes sense not to hold them until later in the game.

Here is what one section near the beginning of the game used to look like (ignore the color):

I think it's a good change and gets to the fun much quicker.

Let me know what you think.

-Jeff

notes.title: Early Access Coming Soon!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35260617/a5ec683ead598eb3bbe525123cddc43818873440.gif[/img]

I know it's been quiet here the last few months, but that will soon be changing.

I have made the decision to release Just Flip to Early Access so those interested can get in, give it a go, and hopefully provide some great feedback as I build out the rest of the game world.

I've been making physics games in my spare time for well over 10 years and I always fall short when it comes to getting pre-release feedback.  I think some aspects of my previous games have suffered because of this.

This time I have decided to do the opposite of what I've done in the past and instead build out the game world with the help of a community.

I resisted this for a while because I didn't think it would be possible given my game dev time is pretty limited: Family, day job, life.  However, I think I found a way to do it.

I've spent the last several months working to get all the important underlying game systems developed and solid.  This should leave mostly world building, the fun stuff, for Early Access.

With the underlying systems in place, I think I can keep a steady flow of content for the Early Access players.  

My ultimate goal is to end up with 1 MASSIVE, continuous mountain world for players to jump, flip, and ski through.  I plan to get there by building smaller sections of the world and releasing them at regular intervals.

I have a lot of ideas for the world, but I'm really excited to get input and ideas from others.  This is my number one reason for releasing to Early Access.

I don't have any actual release date yet, but I'm getting close. 

Stay Tuned and please let me know what you think of the refreshed steam page!

notes.title: Just Flip (and Ski???)
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35260617/0b936b6a55089fdf02efedc5536b1be918fc3a4f.gif[/img]

While I love how the flipping mechanic turned out for "Just Flip", I have started to wonder if it's enough to carry the game.  

I kept having the feeling that the game needed a better "Hook".  Well, I already had a skiing mechanic that people seemed to like in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/740230/Just_Ski__a_physics_game_by_Jeff_Weber/]Just Ski[/url], so why not combine them.

The above is a very rough, down and dirty, prototype of flipping combined with skiing.

I would love to know what you think of the idea.

-Jeff
